Nigerian Army troops have reportedly recovered an AK-47 rifle from the residence of a suspected arms dealer in Wukari Local Government Area of Taraba State.
The weapon was recovered during a joint operation involving personnel of the 6 Brigade Garrison of the Nigerian Army and operatives of the Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA).
The operation, reportedly conducted at about 9:50 p.m. on 13 November, followed the arrest of the suspected arms dealer at Technobat in Jalingo, the state capital, on 20 October.
Security analyst Zagazola Makama disclosed the development in a post on X on Sunday.
According to the report, following the suspect’s arrest, security operatives traced his residence to Wukari, where they conducted a search and discovered the AK-47 rifle.
“The recovered weapon has been taken into military custody for further investigation and necessary action,” Mr Makama said.
The recovery comes amid security concerns over the circulation of illegal firearms and the activities of armed criminal groups in Taraba and neighbouring states.

Security agencies have continued operations aimed at identifying arms suppliers and disrupting networks suspected of providing weapons to criminal groups.
However, the military has yet to publicly disclose the identity of the suspect or provide further details about the circumstances surrounding his arrest.
It is also unclear whether the suspect has been formally charged in court.
